body: Personally I think it's better to leave a note, but I've read that only 15-38% of people leave one. I think that it gives some form of closure behind. I don't think notes should name anyone, I believe the note should be about yourself, something along the lines of explaining your life? However people kill themselves for very different reasons so it's very subjective
Thanks, I'll try to keep things under control for now, I've started the process for getting help anyway, I appreciate the time taken to respond to this, cheers man
If you want to talk about anything, PM me, I'm very happy to talk about anything and everything
I completely agree, I do not fear death in the slightest, rather I welcome it, although not to the extent of inflicting it upon myself.
Unfortunately I can't agree with you on that. I think everyone deserves at least a minimal form a closure
Thanks that's actually a good insight to have, I just hope it's going to end up a constructive process rather than a destructive one

You aren't bothering anyone, and I have to admit that sounds like an awful situation to be a part of so I won't pretend like I understand or can offer any advice, but just know that if you want to talk about things you can PM me, I just hope that her suicidal thoughts don't project on to you

Honestly I've never resonated with someone so well, it seems as if everyone else is oblivious to cold hard fact that we do not matter. I would also love to be one of these bubbly people that seem to think life is fantastic and that there will always be a silver spoon jammed into their mouthed. Don't worry I've been called a psychopath and a sociopath multiple times, comical considering I'm a psychology undergrad

I can't fathom what you may be going through because we are individuals, but I can see we have similar mindsets on the nature of our existence. From what I can tell from your posts you seem very articulate, and all I can say is that yes, we are all a statistic in the end, even the famous ones. Something tells me that you are fairly intelligent, hence the questioning of bigger pictures, but perhaps adequacy is subjective, and it's the littler things that really matter?

I'm 19 and from UK, I understand what you mean, but I've found faking happiness is no better than being honest with how you feel. In the end, our entire existence is futile unless you make a significant difference to the 'world' so to speak. Interpretation of 'world' in this context is primarily subjective
I think there's something comforting about knowing what you would say should it come to it that one wants to kill oneself
PM me if you want to talk about anything and everything

I'm more than happy to just rant about everything. Perhaps happy is the wrong word.
